items.title: Harrison Chase: let one curator agent make all wiki edits
items.takeaway: He says agents, main or sub, can't reliably edit a wiki. A separate curator agent should make every edit. He describes this as common across LangChain's work.
items.soWhat: Give one agent clear ownership of shared knowledge instead of letting every agent write to it.

items.title: Harrison Chase: every internal LangChain agent has a learning loop
items.takeaway: He says all of LangChain's internal agents, for GTM, content and LangSmith Engine, have a learning loop. He links a write-up on what makes a knowledge factory.
items.soWhat: Ask whether your agents get better from their own work or start from zero each time.

items.title: Ryan Carson's team shares Devin Bots that own parts of the app
items.takeaway: He says Devin Bots at HelloUntangle act like employees who own parts of the app and the engineering process. The team keeps one shared list, and everyone talks to the same Bots.
items.soWhat: Shared, named agents with clear ownership are easier to manage than one private agent per person.

items.title: Tibo says his Squad agents now run his Gmail inbox
items.takeaway: He says his Squad agents handle long email threads, ping him for important items and send follow-ups. This is self-reported, with no demo shown.
items.soWhat: Email triage is an early, low-risk place for leaders to test delegating to agents.

hotOnX.text: Uses one tool for about half his work with his 'software factory'; calls it his best experience across desktop, mobile and cloud.
